description:
Observed signal
CI's test job (cargo llvm-cov, run 27749142451) fails matrix::tail_recursion::interp with 'fz2 exceeded 3s'. The same trial passes in ~instant time locally (the whole tail_recursion group runs in ~2.7s without coverage). The fixture drives count(100000, 0) — 100k-deep self-recursion that must TCO — through the interpreter; coverage instrumentation slows the per-step interpreter loop enough to blow the 3s path budget.

This is the same family as the enum_tier0/enum_map_family 'drive limit' CI timeouts: instrumentation overhead masquerading as a logic failure.

Disable
Deferred via 'defer.interp' frontmatter on fixtures2/behavior/tail_recursion.fz, rationale names this ticket. Other modes (run/build) stay live.

Fix — pick the right place, not a per-fixture timeout bump
Decide whether this is pure instrumentation overhead or a real interpreter perf cliff on deep recursion:
- If pure overhead: the holistic fix is to scale the matrix path wall-clock/drive budgets by a coverage factor (detect cfg(coverage)/LLVM_PROFILE_FILE in the harness) so instrumentation can never be read as failure — this also covers enum_tier0/enum_map_family timeout legs.
- If a real cliff: fix the interpreter hot path so 100k TCO iterations stay within budget even instrumented.

Re-enable
Remove the defer.interp line; confirm matrix::tail_recursion::interp is green under both a plain run and cargo llvm-cov.
title: [BUG] tail_recursion::interp exceeds 3s wall-clock only under llvm-cov
